gold_assessment.reasoning: Gold CC notes only wheeze. Generated CC adds shortness of breath and a duration in the chief complaint, so the pure fact 'presents with wheeze' is not cleanly captured alone.
Generated HPI-001 states 2–3 days of wheeze (plus SOB, exertional). The duration of wheeze matches the gold fact.
Gold: no fever, temperature 37 °C. Generated HPI-003 and asm-002 characterize 37 °C as a subjective/low-grade fever, which conflicts with 'no fever'.
Gold mentions cold symptoms; the generated facts do not reference cold/URI symptoms.

Gold: not coughing up sputum (no sputum production). Generated HPI-002: 'frequent nonproductive cough'—this implies presence of cough rather than its absence; also ROS-002 focuses on sputum production only, not on cough. So the absence of cough is contradicted by presence of frequent cough.
Gold: denies haemoptysis and chest pain. Generated ROS-001 and ROS-003 explicitly deny chest pain and hemoptysis.
Gold: not waking at night due to symptoms. Generated ROS-004: 'no nocturnal symptoms.' These are equivalent.
Gold: currently not exercising. No generated fact addresses exercise cessation or current exercise habits.

Gold: sometimes can't complete sentences but no SOB at rest. Generated HPI-004: sometimes cannot finish sentences when exerting. Partial but clinically equivalent for the positive component; the rest-at-rest detail is omitted but not contradicted.
Gold: no problems walking upstairs. Generated facts mention exertional worsening but do not specify stairs or lack of difficulty with stairs.
Gold: more wheezy walking to work. Generated HPI-001: symptoms worsen with exertion/walking. This captures the exertional worsening though not specifically 'to work', but conceptually aligned.
Gold: doesn't have peak-flow meter at home. Generated HPI-005 states no peak flow monitoring at home, matching this.
Gold: missed a few days of work. Generated SH-005: has missed work / works from home due to symptoms. This includes missed work and is consistent, with extra detail.
Gold: history of asthma since childhood. Generated PMH-001 just notes asthma history, without specifying since childhood.
Gold: prior hospital admissions for asthma, no ITU. Generated HPI-007: prior hospital visits for asthma not requiring ICU. This matches.
Gold: hayfever. Generated PMH-002: history of hay fever (allergic rhinitis).
Gold: eczema. Generated PMH-003: history of eczema.
Gold: intermittently uses salbutamol every few weeks. Generated MED-001 and HPI-006: salbutamol inhaler used intermittently/about every few weeks. Matches.
Gold: needs salbutamol when exercising. Generated facts do not state that salbutamol is specifically needed with exercise.
Gold: stopped regular asthma medication 3–4 years ago. Generated HPI-008 says 'asthma improved/stopped ~3–4 years ago' (symptom course), not explicitly that medications were stopped then.
Gold: no known drug allergies. Generated ALLERGY-001: no known drug allergies.
Gold: non-smoker. Generated SH-001: does not smoke.
Gold: 1 unit alcohol every 2–3 days. Generated SH-002: one glass of wine every 2–3 days. This is consistent and reasonably equivalent although different unit description.
Gold: lives with partner. Generated SH-003: lives with partner.
Gold: works as engineer. Generated SH-004: occupation engineer.
Gold: impression—exacerbation of asthma. Generated ASM-001: most likely diagnosis asthma exacerbation causing acute wheeze/SOB. Matches.

Gold: advise continue to monitor temperature and call if fever spikes. Generated plan mentions monitoring and escalation in context of worsening including temperature (PLAN-005, PLAN-008), but not explicitly 'continue to monitor temperature and contact if spiking'; it’s reframed as immediate care for high temperature and antipyretics. This alters nuance and does not cleanly restate the gold instruction.
Gold: collect prescription for peak-flow meter and spacer. Generated PLAN-001 and PLAN-002: prescribe peak flow meter and spacer. The action of issuing/collecting prescription is captured.
Gold: pharmacist will advise on usage. Generated PLAN-002 and PLAN-006 both specify pharmacist demonstration/technique teaching. This aligns.
Gold: record PEFR twice daily, on waking and at night. Generated PLAN-004: record peak flow morning and evening daily for the next week. Same schedule with added duration; covered.

Gold: increase salbutamol with spacer to 2–4 puffs every 4 hours. Generated PLAN-003: salbutamol 2–4 puffs inhaled every 4 hours while symptomatic. Matches the dosing/frequency with slight extra condition.
Gold: may need to add another inhaler. Generated PLAN-010: plan to consider starting controller inhaler at follow-up. This is a more specific form of adding another inhaler and is consistent.
Gold: advised regular antihistamine. Generated PLAN-009: recommend regular oral antihistamine. This matches.
Gold: arrange review next week. Generated FU-001: arrange review in about one week (via telephone/telemedicine). Same timing; extra modality detail only.

Gold: if wheeze not settling/worsening and feels unwell, seek urgent appointment. Generated PLAN-005: seek immediate care if worsening wheeze/SOB, inability to complete sentences, high temperature, or other deterioration. This covers and expands the gold criteria for urgent review.

gen_assessment.reasoning: Gold CC only mentions wheeze; there is no chief-complaint documentation of SOB or explicit 2–3 day duration there. SOB and timing in CC are additional details.
2–3 days of wheeze matches the gold HPI. Added SOB and exertional worsening are additions but not contradictions; exertional worsening is consistent with 'more wheezy walking to work' (hpi-010).

Gold HPI notes not coughing up sputum and does not describe a frequent cough. Generated fact asserts frequent nonproductive cough, introducing a symptom that the gold record omits and implies absence of cough; this conflicts with the gold description.
Gold explicitly states no fever with a measured 37 °C. Generated fact calls 37 °C a 'subjective fever', which reverses the gold characterization.

Gold: sometimes can't complete sentences but no SOB at rest. Generated: sometimes cannot finish sentences when exerting. This is consistent with the exertional limitation component; it omits the 'no SOB at rest' part but does not contradict it.
Gold: doesn't have peak flow meter at home. Generated: no peak flow monitoring at home. Same substantive point.
Gold: sometimes takes salbutamol every few weeks. Generated: intermittently about every few weeks. This is aligned.
Gold: prior hospital admissions for asthma, no ITU. Generated: prior hospital visits for asthma not requiring ICU. Equivalent.

Gold specifies asthma since childhood and that medications were stopped 3–4 years ago, but does not state that the asthma itself improved or stopped at that time. Generated statement interprets symptom course and is not directly supported.
Gold: denies chest pain. Generated ROS-001: denies chest pain. Same finding, differently sectioned.
Gold: not coughing up sputum. Generated: denies sputum production. Matches the sputum-related component.
Gold: denies haemoptysis. Generated: denies hemoptysis. Same information.
Gold: not night-time waking. Generated: no nocturnal symptoms. These are equivalent in context of asthma symptoms.
Gold: history of asthma as a child. Generated: history of asthma. The generated fact is less specific but consistent.
Gold: hayfever. Generated: history of hay fever (allergic rhinitis). Same condition.
Gold: eczema. Generated: history of eczema. Matches.
Gold: sometimes uses salbutamol every few weeks. Generated: current salbutamol inhaler used intermittently. This aligns, though dosing details are not specified.
Gold: NKDA. Generated: no known drug allergies. Same.
Gold: non-smoker. Generated: does not smoke. Consistent.
Gold: 1 unit alcohol every 2–3 days. Generated: one glass of wine every 2–3 days. Roughly equivalent alcohol intake; no contradiction.
Gold: lives with partner. Generated: lives with partner.
Gold: works as engineer. Generated: occupation engineer.
Gold: has missed a few days of work. Generated: has missed work/works from home due to symptoms. This supports and extends the gold fact.
Gold: recorded temp 37 °C. Generated: temperature 37 °C. Same objective measure, although gold clarifies no fever.
Gold: impression—exacerbation asthma. Generated: most likely diagnosis asthma exacerbation causing acute wheeze/SOB. Same assessment with added description.

Gold characterizes the temperature as 'no fever' with temp 37 °C. Generated fact interprets 37 °C as a low-grade fever possibly due to viral illness or inflammation, which conflicts with the explicit 'no fever'.
Gold notes hayfever but does not state that chronic allergic rhinitis contributes to airway hyperreactivity. That causal interpretation is an added clinical inference.
Gold lists current/previous asthma meds and that they were stopped 3–4 years ago but does not state 'incomplete documentation' or 'possible suboptimal control'. These are interpretive additions.
Gold: collect prescription for peak-flow meter. Generated: prescribe a peak flow meter for home monitoring. The prescribing/obtaining of a device is the same plan element.

Gold: collect prescription of peak flow meter and spacer; pharmacist can advise on usage. Generated: prescribe spacer and arrange pharmacist demonstration. This aligns with spacer prescription and education.
Gold: increase salbutamol with spacer to 2–4 puffs 4-hourly. Generated: advise salbutamol 2–4 puffs every 4 hours while symptomatic. Same regimen with an added condition.
Gold: record PEFR twice daily, first on waking and at night. Generated: record peak flow morning and evening daily for the next week. Same timing; adds duration of one week.

Gold: if wheeze not settling/getting worse and feels unwell, seek urgent appointment. Generated: seek immediate care with worsening wheeze/increasing SOB, inability to complete sentences, high temperature, or other deterioration. This is a more detailed but consistent escalation plan.
Gold: pharmacist can advise on usage of peak flow meter and spacer. Generated: pharmacist to demonstrate spacer and peak flow technique. Equivalent action.

Gold does include some education elements (monitor temperature, use devices, follow-up) but does not explicitly state a broad educational plan about inhaler use, spacer benefits, and indications for urgent care as a grouped educational intervention. This is a synthesized addition.
Gold plan does not mention antipyretics or symptomatic management for fever. Recommendation of antipyretics is an added management detail.
Gold: advised to take regular antihistamine. Generated: recommend regular oral antihistamine. Same plan with route specified.
Gold: may need to add in another inhaler. Generated: plan to reassess and consider starting a controller inhaler. This is a specific form of adding another inhaler and consistent with the intent.
Gold: arrange review next week. Generated: arrange review in about one week (telephone/telemedicine) to evaluate peak flow and therapy needs. Same timing with extra details on modality and purpose.
